summary: Cycle 13 observed: 24 of 27 hold. ladders-work now holds: the water climb, the swim-in, the shaft climb to the road, and the strict descent (taken over the hatch at 358 ms, ridden down with no sample off the ladder, let go standing on the cap at -330). Open: respawn-works (the respawn is right — 5.7 s, 95 px from the moved checkpoint, standing 3 s later — but the probe judged 'at the checkpoint' 3 s on, after a knock along the catwalk), enemies-path (2 of 3: the player held for 20.5 game seconds; hunters that close are blocked by the 140 px shaft hatches the AI cannot cross), frame-cost (4.76x, the player held at every spot).

claims.text: ladders-work holds: downTrail [2060,-860,0] -> [2008,-837,1] ... [1980,-416,1] -> [1980,-330,0]: taken over the hatch, down at up to 340 px/s, let go at the foot standing (down: feet -330, ladder 0). The water trail and the swim-in trail take the ladder on arrival. The tracked hold fixed the foot.

respawn-works: gone -> back in 5.7 s; the first sample alive was x 13345, feet -330 — 95 px from the checkpoint now on the catwalk (13440) — and 3 s later x 13180, feet -330, standing on the catwalk. The probe's atCheckpoint read the 3-s-later place (a knock along the floor under fire), while the property is where the respawn puts the player. The review's wording was 'back within 8 s and within 150 px of the checkpoint': judged at the first moment back.

enemies-path: with the player held at the bait (20.5 game s over 30.6 wall s; 5 put-backs; no deaths; never in a vehicle), movedCount 2 (the road marksman closed 211, the road trooper 152) and anyMoved 7; the rest went away: a deck trooper 875 px off, the heavy 1475 east, a cap trooper into the sea.

The 140 px shaft hatches cut the AI's floors (operator's scratch run outside the store, the soldiers' positions every 8 s): the deck trooper west of the bait walked into the hatch at 5580 (5510-5650, between it and the player), fell through to the cap and into the sea; the road trooper stood at the road's hatch pressing down. The soldiers don't use the mod's ladders, and a walker falls into a 140 px hole. The hatches were widened (cycle 6) so a climber's body wouldn't snag their edges — since then a climber collides with nothing, so the hole only needs to show the way: 30 px, which walkers cross in their stride (the pontoon's hatch). The narrowed level lints clean (all objectives reachable, 62 ladder links).

frame-cost: perf with the player held at every spot (0 deaths, on foot, within the spot before and after): baseline 133; start 517 (320 draws), tower span 633 (688), deck 617 (621), road 383 (263): 4.76x. 34-46 soldiers asleep at each spot, 35-45 characters hidden off camera for the render. The cost is where the awake soldiers are.

Next: the mod with 30 px hatches (every shaft: the legs, the tower, the cliff, the bunker), baked; the play probe judging the respawn's place at the first moment back (and the descent loop ending once off the ladder at the foot; the bunker eye shot off the basement hatch); the in-loop frame matrix staged, to run the cycle after.

unknowns: Whether the heavy's eastward walk is caused by the hatches (a path around) or by its own hunting of another threat.
